📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that liveKit is building the infrastructure layer for the agentic era of computing. Our platform gives developers everything they need to build, test, deploy, scale, and observe AI agents in production. Founded in 2021, LiveKit powers voice and agentic AI applications for OpenAI, Salesforce, Spotify, Meta, and tens of thousands of other developers, collectively facilitating billions of calls each year.

We're hiring a Solutions Architect (Pre-Sales) to be the technical partner to the engineers and enterprises building on LiveKit.

You'll work alongside an account executive to understand what a customer is trying to build, design the right architecture, and bring it to life with live demos and proofs-of-concept — guiding teams from first conversation to production.

This role is ideal for someone who loves to build, is energized by talking with other engineers, and takes pride in turning a hard technical problem into something that just works. Real-time voice and video is visceral — latency, quality, and reliability are felt, not read about — so the best conversations include something live. You'll collaborate closely with our Sales, Engineering, Product teams to win technical decisions and to make sure what you hear in the field informs how we build.

love to build and solve the most challenging customer problems with LiveKit.

have a curious mind with a continuous desire to learn and improve.

enjoy demoing and presenting, whether to a room or engineer, to a CTO or at a conference.

have a team first mentality, seeking to lift others around you as you progress in your career.

Partner with an account executive as the technical lead on strategic deals — from discovery and architecture design through demos, POCs, and technical decisions.

Advise customers on cloud architecture and deployment across self-hosted and LiveKit Cloud (AWS, GCP, Azure).

Build live demos and reference applications — voice agents, video pipelines, telephony integrations — tailored to each customer's use case, and reusable by the wider team.

Scope and run proofs-of-concept against clear, shared success criteria, guiding customers all the way to production.

Reason with customers about connectivity, infrastructure, and end-to-end latency to design for scale and reliability.

Create technical content — blog posts, guides, webinars, and conference talks — that helps developers and enterprises build with LiveKit.

Act as the technical enabler for your region's pod, and share field insight with Product and Engineering to help shape the roadmap.

4+ years in solutions architecture, sales engineering, or a customer-facing engineering role (or equivalent hands-on engineering experience with strong customer instincts).

Hands-on experience with at least one major cloud provider (AWS, GCP, or Azure) — you can architect, deploy, and debug real applications.

Comfortable with the modern deployment toolchain: containers, Kubernetes, infrastructure-as-code, and networking fundamentals (load balancing, DNS, firewalls/NAT).

Able to reason about connectivity, infrastructure, and latency end to end — how architecture, network path, compute, co-location, and model choice shape the AI agentic experiences of today.

Strong programming ability in at least one of our core SDK languages — Python, TypeScript/Node, or Go.

A clear communicator who can demo, present, and write for technical audiences.

Working knowledge of real-time media protocols and their latency/quality trade-offs (WebRTC, RTP/SRTP, WebSockets).

Familiarity with the AI voice stack: STT/TTS providers, LLM integration, speech-to-speech models, turn detection, and telephony/SIP.

Experience speaking at meetups or conferences, or a track record of technical writing or open-source contributions.

An opportunity to build something truly impactful to the world.

Contribute to open source alongside world-class engineers.

Competitive salary and equity package.

Health, dental, and vision benefits.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Uscreen is the video monetization platform for businesses building recurring revenue from video content. Our customers replace a patchwork stack of separate hosting, community, courses, email, and app vendors with one branded experience across web, mobile, and TV.

Recent findings suggest that the platform is only half of it. We believe growth requires behavior, not just software. Customers don't stall because a feature is missing. They stall because they priced wrong, never built an email list, or rolled out an offer nobody wanted. Coaching is how we fix that, and it's part of the product rather than an add-on.

You own a segment, and you run it like a growth marketer.

Industry observers note that we have a cohort of smaller video businesses where retention is not where it should be. Nobody owns it today. You will. The revenue that stays in that segment, and the revenue that grows inside it, is yours.

This is a coaching role for someone with a growth marketer's mindset. We wouldn't hire a demand gen marketer who couldn't analyze the state of the business and figure out what's needed, and we won't hire a coach who can't either. You'll look at a customer's business the way an owner would: where the revenue comes from, where it leaks, and what to do next. You pull your own numbers to get there. When a customer needs a custom report to answer a growth question, you build it yourself.

Sources indicate that it's a one-to-many job. Your cohort is larger than a 1:1 book, so the work is designing coaching that scales: cohort programs, group sessions, office hours, and triggered outreach when the data states a business is drifting. You'll build that motion rather than inherit it.

It has been revealed that success is measured in dollars: gross revenue retention in your cohort first, expansion second. Not tickets closed, not calls booked.

Industry observers note that A coach with a growth marketer's mindset. Maybe you've run growth or demand gen for a small business, built your own audience, or coached founders through their numbers. You understand how a membership business makes money, you pull your own analytics to see what's working, and you're comfortable doing it in front of a client. What matters is that you can find the real constraint in a business, then sit with the operator and say the honest thing.

Facebook is paying college creators to post Reels

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Back in March, Facebook doubled down on its efforts to woo creators from other platforms by launching Creator Fast Track—a program that pays established creators up to $3,000 a month (for a max of three months) to start posting Reels on Facebook.
  • It has been revealed that now, the Meta-owned platform is expanding that initiative to include U.S.
  • College students with larger followings can also access bonuses that provide “three months of guaranteed pay for sharing eligible reels.” According to Meta, “Creators with at least 20,000 followers on Instagram, TikTok, or YouTube can earn between $100-$450 per month, those with at least 100,000 followers can earn $1,000 per month, and those with more than one million followers can earn $3,000 per month.”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Back in March, Facebook doubled down on its efforts to woo creators from other platforms by launching Creator Fast Track—a program that pays established creators up to $3,000 a month (for a max of three months) to start posting Reels on Facebook.

It has been revealed that now, the Meta-owned platform is expanding that initiative to include U.S. college students with as few as 1,000 followers on Instagram, TikTok, or YouTube. Among other perks, Creator Fast Track College Edition offers eligible creators “immediate access to Facebook Content Monetization” and “increased reach on eligible reels” (per Meta).

College students with larger followings can also access bonuses that provide “three months of guaranteed pay for sharing eligible reels.” According to Meta, “Creators with at least 20,000 followers on Instagram, TikTok, or YouTube can earn between $100-$450 per month, those with at least 100,000 followers can earn $1,000 per month, and those with more than one million followers can earn $3,000 per month.”.

Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

It has been revealed that facebook’s creator payouts hit an all-time high last year at almost $3 billion—a 35% increase from 2024 (per Meta). Reels accounted for 60% of that total, while the rest went to Stories, photos, and text posts.

That growing investment in creators—especially short-form video creators—is clear evidence of Facebook’s determination to compete more directly with rivals like TikTok and YouTube.

And it’s not just targeting massive-name creators, either; as Creator Fast Track’s lower entry point for college students demonstrates, Facebook is eager to attract young creators at the start of their careers.

In a recent development, the rising importance of NIL rights and trends like #RushTok and #DormTok makes that a smart move. Since 2021, student athletes have carved out a bigger and bigger space for themselves in the creator economy, attracting the attention of major brands and platforms.

Content creation has also become a strong Plan B for NIL athletes who may not go pro after college. If Facebook can become a key platform for those creators while they’re still in school, it has a better shot at keeping them around after graduation—whether they go pro or pivot to full-time content creation.

Whatnot and Meta are taking aim at TikTok Shop’s Black Friday crown

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (541 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tubefilter

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Black Friday is almost here, and platforms are eager to claim their share of the shopping frenzy—and hopefully replicate the success TikTok Shop has seen over the last two years.
  • Recent findings suggest that in 2024, creators hosted over 30,000 live shopping streams on TikTok Shop—and some walked away with millions in sales.
  • Canvas Beauty itself ended up selling 100,000+ products and making $3 million in sales over the course of the day, it told Business Insider.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Black Friday is almost here, and platforms are eager to claim their share of the shopping frenzy—and hopefully replicate the success TikTok Shop has seen over the last two years.

Recent findings suggest that in 2024, creators hosted over 30,000 live shopping streams on TikTok Shop—and some walked away with millions in sales. Stormi Steele, founder/CEO of hair/skincare brand Canvas Beauty, spotlighted her own brand in a TikTok livestream on Black Friday and made more than $2 million from viewers buying products off the broadcast.

Canvas Beauty itself ended up selling 100,000+ products and making $3 million in sales over the course of the day, it told Business Insider.

Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

In a recent development, that trend picked up speed in 2025, with sellers and creators hosting over 760,000 livestream sessions across TikTok Shop’s Black Friday/Cyber Monday campaign (per TikTok). By hauling in over $500 million of U.S. sales between Black Friday and Cyber Monday, the ecommerce hub averaged over $125 million of daily sales across the four-day period.

TikTok, of course, is hoping to top that performance in 2026—and it seems well on its way to pulling it off. The platform reported that U.S. live shopping sales on Shop more than doubled in the first half of this year (as compared to the first half of 2025), and TikTok Shop President for Strategic Initiatives Patrick Nommensen added that hashtags like #holidayshopping rose 263% in September.

Shop’s 2026 Black Friday/Cyber Monday holiday campaign began November 11 and is set to run until November 30, with top brands like Best Buy, Ulta Beauty, Sephora, Michael Kors, and Victoria’s Secret expected to take part (per Retail Brew).

To keep viewers locked in on its Black Friday offerings, TikTok Shop will need to compete with Facebook Marketplace and Instagram, which eMarketer claims dominate roughly three-quarters of U.S. social commerce.

That’s a significant lead, but Meta isn’t resting on its laurels. Last week, Instagram introduced a newly introduced tool that lets creators add Amazon affiliate links directly to Reels and feed posts. As reported by Business Insider, an additional integration allows creators to link to products from Halara, Lowe’s and Shein.

It has been revealed that youTube is heading into its first holiday season with Amazon in its Shopping affiliate program, too. Since late August, eligible U.S. creators have been able to tag products from the ecommerce juggernaut in their Shorts, long-form videos, and livestreams.

Sources indicate that not to be left out of the Black Friday push, Whatnot has confirmed aims to drop its sales cut to the “lowest level of the year,” with 0% commission for all sellers on Black Friday and again for eligible small sellers on November 28. Major creator collabs will also draw viewers to the live shopping platform, with MrBeast, Shay Mitchell, Kai Cenat, Claudia Oshry, Ben Soffer, David Dobrik, and other top stars hosting exclusive highlights from November 27-30.

Whatnot’s announcement post includes a blurb detailing “why Black Friday is better on Whatnot for shoppers”—but we’ll be keeping an eye out to see which platform actually comes out on top once the weekend wraps up.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Google, which makes billions of dollars a year thanks to YouTubers stocking its platform with billions of hours of videos, is envisioning a future where we don’t need content creators.

    According to 404 Media, the tech giant has filed a patent for something called “My Channel“: a 24/7 feed of AI-generated videos tailored specifically to every individual user’s preferences.

    If put into practice, Google would take everything it knows about a person–which, between Google’s far-reaching ad biz, Android phones, Google Maps, and YouTube watch history, is a lot–and get (presumably) Veo to spool out an endless stream of content.

    Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

    Recent findings suggest that but we’re not just talking any content. Google’s key selling point here is that you–yes, you–can star in all of your slop channel’s videos.

    It has been revealed that “You are a customized video generating model. Generate a customized video for a user where the user will play the protagonist,” Google says in an example prompt filed with the patent application. “The generated customized video includes characteristics based on the . The generated customized video follows the style and format of the of the user. The generated customized video sticks to the of the user but the narrative for the generated customized video is customized. The and parameters are ordered from more preferred to less preferred.”.

    404 Media reports the patent notes My Channels will be connected to an “advertising server” that will “[generate] an updated customized media content item by inserting at least one advertisement into the customized media content item.”.

    Basically, it wants to put a fake you into fake videos as their “protagonist,” and then you’ll have to watch real ads to see the fake you in the fake videos.

    Does this necessarily mean everyone who has a My Channel will stop watching human creators? No. But a 24/7 channel of customized catnip will drain at least some watch time toward these siloed slop-factories, and away from humans who make actual content (and rely on views for income).

    As for the sorts of videos Google’s AI will generate, the patent filing included examples like “a crime/comedy caper,” “a fun romantic comedy,” “a sci-fi adventure,” and “an action/thriller experience,” all of which would be slopped out for a viewer named “John.”.

    According to recent reports, in another example, the “protagonist” is a viewer who likes cricket. If Google’s system noticed this person watching a video about a certain player’s gangbuster performance during a recent cricket match, it could then generate a video “that incorporates elements of the Cricket World Cup and Player 1’s recent performance,” the filing claims. “Perhaps [user_name] could be cheering for India in the stands or interacting with Player 1 in some way.”.

    As 404 Media points out, numerous proponents of gen AI have spent years crowing about the potential for personalized entertainment. Didn’t like how Stranger Things ended? Generate your ending. Third movie in a series got cancelled? Just ‘make’ it yourself. News coverage didn’t agree with your opinion? Your chatbot’s ready with a newly introduced broadcast. It sounds dystopian, because it is. It also seemed far-fetched, three years ago.

    Recent findings suggest that this is a future we’ve already been pitched. It’s just that once, the pitch was a Black Mirror episode. Now it’s Google’s business model.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that last month, Roblox ushered in Halloween with a platform-wide horror event stocked with mazes, monsters, and general mayhem. That nine-night event—called The Hollow—featured creepy creatures from a variety of well-known Roblox experiences, including 99 Nights in the Forest, DOORS, Dandy’s World, Scary Shawarma Kiosk, and more.

    Now, Roblox is switching gears from horror to family-friendly holiday fun. Ahead of Thanksgiving, the platform is inviting players to express their gratitude by building something tall—“like, really tall.”.

    Sources indicate that starting tomorrow, the sandbox platform will kick off The Great Build: a global community event culminating in the creation of “a massive tower of gratitude.” According to a press release, the event will run through Nov. 30 and is designed to encourage players around the world to “share what they’re thankful for and work together toward a shared goal.”.

    Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

    The process is as simple as it is wholesome. Every hour, players will receive a free block that they can personalize with a message “inspired by gratitude traditions from around the world” and add to the tower, Roblox claims.

    Players can also climb The Great Build as it grows, and will unlock free avatar items as different community milestones are achieved.

    A gratitude-themed event aimed at global unity is exactly the kind of positive PR Roblox needs right now.

    According to Latin Times, the sandbox platform is at the moment facing almost 200 consolidated federal lawsuits, with states and parents alike pushing back against the platform’s approach to child safety.

    It has been revealed that legislators are bearing down on Roblox, too. Earlier this month, Senators Josh Hawley and Dick Durbin proposed the “No Forced Arbitration for Child Sexual Exploitation and Cyber Injuries Act,” which would allow families to take Roblox to court regardless of forced arbitration terms.

    The “first-ever congressional hearing on Roblox safety” followed the bill’s introduction and included appearances from both legal experts and survivors of child sexual exploitation.

    Roblox CEO David Baszucki, on the other hand, reportedly sent a “last-minute letter instead of testifying before the Senate subcommittee.” We’re guessing the platform’s Thanksgiving tower of gratitude won’t be quite tall enough to overshadow that absence.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    But the overall-clad creator isn’t just helping tots reach their learning milestones online—she’s also advocating for children caught up in the U.S. immigration system.

    On Monday, Ms Rachel (aka Rachel Accurso) joined U.S. Representative-elect Brad Lander at an immigration court in Upcoming York City to support children expected to take part in legal hearings without attorneys.

    Daily industry updates, straight to your inbox.

    Accurso posted a video of the visit on Instagram, where she wrote that “Kids representing themselves in immigration court is so wrong… I saw Angel up at the mic without a lawyer and I couldn’t believe it. He’s 9 years old! Hearing kids hear the word ‘removable’ over and over about themselves… Heartbreaking.”.

    A nine-year-old appearing in court without a lawyer may seem unfathomable, but Angel is far from the only child representing himself within a deeply complicated immigration system.

    Earlier this year, the Trump administration failed to renew a contract “with a nationwide network of legal service providers that represented thousands of unaccompanied minors in immigration court” (per the Times Union). While Governor Kathy Hochul announced state funding to combat the sudden gap in resources, Fresh York still has “the third-largest unaccompanied minors caseload in the nation” with nearly 10,000 open cases as of August 2026.

    As severe as Upcoming York’s backlog is, it’s just one part of a nationwide crisis—and Accurso isn’t limiting her advocacy to the East Coast.

    Recent findings suggest that just a few days before appearing at the Ted Weiss Federal Building in NYC, the creator used her expansive online platform to spotlight a conversation with Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa. In a video shared on Instagram, Hinojosa shared her plan to end family immigration detention—a cause Accurso herself has vocally championed.

    Advocacy on multiple fronts has long been a key part of Accurso’s online presence, despite repeated backlash from right-wing critics and parents over her support for the LGBTQ+ community and Palestinian children impacted by the war in Gaza.

    The creator’s contributions to the latter cause include a 2024 campaign that raised $50,000 for Save the Children’s Emergency Fund and, more recently, a $1 million pledge to the Palestine Children’s Relief Fund.

    It has been revealed that now, as Accurso fights for the rights of minors in U.S. courtrooms and detention centers, she’s demonstrating once again that all children are welcome in Ms Rachel’s classroom.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • LiveKit is building the infrastructure layer for the voice-driven era of computing.
    • Most product designers want to design for everyone.
    • You'll thrive as a Senior Product Designer if you:.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    LiveKit is building the infrastructure layer for the voice-driven era of computing. Our platform gives developers everything they need to build, test, deploy, scale, and observe agents in production. Founded in 2021, LiveKit powers voice AI applications for OpenAI, xAI, Salesforce, Coursera, Spotify, and thousands of others, collectively facilitating billions of calls each year.

    Most product designers want to design for everyone. This role is for someone who'd rather design for one very specific, very opinionated person: the developer at 2am trying to figure out why their voice agent just failed a call. You'll design the tools developers use to test, evaluate and debug AI agents — a category that's still being invented, with no established patterns to copy. If dense data, real-time systems and reading a stack trace sound more fun than intimidating, keep reading.

    You'll thrive as a Senior Product Designer if you:.

    are obsessed with making the best product for our customers.

    are known as the go-to person for tackling tough problems.

    work hard and can build and ship fast.

    are focused on polish, detail and quality.

    are a fast learner, frequently picking up new tips, tricks, and skills.

    The best way to impress us is with thoughtful ways you'd implement LiveKit, and potentially tinkering with it 😊.

    Own the design of how developers test, evaluate and observe their agents — simulations, evals, logs and agent insights.

    Turn complex, real-time data into interfaces that are easy to scan, understand and act on.

    Design upcoming interaction patterns for AI-native workflows, where agents generate the first draft and humans adjust it.

    Prototype in code and work hand-in-hand with engineers to ship polished work.

    Contribute patterns to our design system for dense, debugging-oriented surfaces.

    You've shipped design work for developer tools, observability or data-heavy products.

    You have strong data-visualization instincts and know when a chart beats a table (and when it doesn't).

    You're comfortable in code — reading PRs, tweaking Tailwind, building prototypes.

    You earn the trust of deeply technical users and engineers.

    Experience designing for AI or agent tooling.

    AI tools are already a core part of how you design.

    An opportunity to build something truly impactful to the world.

    Contribute to open source alongside world-class engineers.

    Competitive salary and equity package.

    Health, dental, and vision benefits.

    LiveKit is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of any characteristic protected by applicable law. If you require a reasonable accommodation during the application or interview process, please contact recruiting@livekit.io.

    • Our Dashboard is a primary tool for configuring our components, as well as a centralized place for managing your app’s consumers.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Clerk is on a mission to solve user management once and for all. We are a globally distributed team dedicated to providing best-in-class developer experience, with obsessive attention to every detail. Today, we provide developers with full-stack React components and hooks like , , , useUser, and useOrganization. These APIs allow developers to build hard-to-get-right user and organization management flows. We believe that a component is worth a thousand APIs.

    Our Dashboard is a primary tool for configuring our components, as well as a centralized place for managing your app’s consumers.

    You’ll join Visual Designers, UI Engineers, and fellow Product Designers on the Clerk Design team to build our core product, the Clerk Dashboard. You’ll always keep developer experience first as you gain a deeper understanding of the business needs of user management. You’ll optimize for customer delight, flexibility, and ease-of-use within a complicated, technical domain.

    Recent findings suggest that collaborate with teammates to design newly introduced features. You’ll work closely with Product, Design, and Engineering across project lifecycles from ideation to implementation.

    Gather requirements. You’ll research the technology and customer impetus behind the features we release. You’ll attain a deep understanding of the problems we solve.

    Structure and prototype. You’ll create flows and interactions that make sense of complex information, whether it’s a static component or a multi-page view.

    Not settle for less than pixel-perfection. You’ll work with a world-class UI Engineering team to bring your Figma frames to life. You set the bar for quality.

    Elevate our design culture. You’ll support and expand the Clerk Design visual language, component library, accessibility practices, design system, and design processes.

    You’re a Senior(+) level Product Designer with experience working in authentication, user management, or developer tools. You love your craft. You push Engineers to build experiences they’re unsure if they’re capable of (and you expect them to do the same for you).

    According to recent reports, you’re in the Americas. The Clerk Design team is spread across the globe; Product Design right now spans UTC+1 to UTC+5:30. You live in a location that is ±3 hours within U.S. Mountain Time (MDT, UTC−06:00).

    You have technical fluency. You have a deep understanding of designing interactive software on the web. You don’t need to author production-ready front-end code, but it’s a major plus if you can.

    You work iteratively. Your process embodies a “ship and iterate” mentality. You value the quick pace of a growing startup like Clerk.

    You own your time. You’re a self-starter who would rather find a tough problem to solve instead of waiting for a new task. To be successful at Clerk, you need to make the most of the autonomy you’re given.

    💰 Competitive Salary – We want you to know that we value the skills and experience you bring to the table. We go out of our way to make sure that you feel fairly compensated.

    It has been revealed that 📈 Equity Ownership – At Clerk, we believe in shared success. That's why we offer a stock option plan so that everyone can benefit from the growth and prosperity of the tech giant.

    Recent findings suggest that ⚕️ Health Coverage – We care about your well-being. That's why we offer top-tier health insurance to ensure that your health needs are fully met.

    Sources indicate that 🎧 Work Gear - Set up your ideal home office with the gear of your choice. At Clerk, we want to ensure that you have everything you need to perform at your best.

    Industry observers note that 🏖️ Flexible Vacation Policy – We believe in work-life balance and trust you to take the time you need. Although we recommend 25 days per year, our vacation policy is unlimited. This is in addition to observing national holidays specific to your country of residence.

    Sources indicate that 🌍 Diverse and Inclusive Team – Join our exceptional, diverse, and globally distributed team at Clerk. We are committed to fostering an inclusive environment where everyone can contribute their best in building impactful products and tools for the modern web.

    #113435. Most AI Citations That Disappeared Came Back, Study Finds via @sejournal, @MattGSouthern

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (2028 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Searchenginejournal ↗ Open Full Page

    Most AI Citations That Disappeared Came Back, Study Finds via @sejournal, @MattGSouthern

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2028 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Searchenginejournal

    ⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Around three in four AI citation drops were temporary, according to Ahrefs’ study of the changes in five different AI products over 20 days.
    • It has been revealed that when sharing AI citation analysis results with clients or bosses, you should be aware that a loss may not represent what it seems like at first glance.
    • Ahrefs studied about 37,500 first-day citations made by Google’s AI Mode and AI Overviews, along with ChatGPT, Gemini and Copilot.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Around three in four AI citation drops were temporary, according to Ahrefs’ study of the changes in five different AI products over 20 days.

    It has been revealed that when sharing AI citation analysis results with clients or bosses, you should be aware that a loss may not represent what it seems like at first glance. Sites in the study that had been cited in answers but then dropped out of those answers were more likely to have another citation occur for them as opposed to staying missing. If someone rewrote a page in the meantime, that rewrite could receive credit for a citation it didn’t earn.

    Ahrefs studied about 37,500 first-day citations made by Google’s AI Mode and AI Overviews, along with ChatGPT, Gemini and Copilot. The study included only one organization’s view based on its own group of questions answered daily by each tool for 20 days.

    The study’s findings point to four items to look into before making an edit to a webpage based upon the disappearance of a citation.

    Tracking the same citations for consecutive days, the study was able to see what can happen after a site has disappeared from an answer.

    Industry observers note that these results were documented by Mateusz Makosiewicz, an SEO and marketing educator at Ahrefs. His colleague Xibeijia Guan collected all websites that had been cited on day one, then traced each reference through to day 20.

    By day two, about half of those references were gone from AI Overviews. Even more were gone on each of the other tools. Most of these returned prior to the conclusion of the study.

    Across the five tools, about half of the citations that dropped out came back within three days, Ahrefs found.

    The data collected in this study reflects the number of websites, thus when a website comes back, this study cannot determine whether the exact same webpage came back as well.

    Industry observers note that another measure was taken (in Brand Radar’s own tracking of citations), revealing a somewhat comparable pattern with lower rates of return. About two-thirds of all the citations that disappeared from view there ultimately did come back. Ahrefs sells Brand Radar, and the write-up has a section on using it.

    Earlier research I have discussed demonstrated changes in AI responses over multiple runs of a prompt, and this current study adds what happens across different days.

    I reported on SparkToro’s findings in January regarding their discovery that both ChatGPT and Google’s AI in Search provided the same list of brands less than 1% of the time across repeated runs of the same prompt. They also found that the frequency with which a brand appeared throughout multiple runs was generally more stable than the specific ranking of that brand within those lists.

    The fresh study’s authors recommend counting how many of the last seven days a site was cited. This is a frequency count by day for the sites that were cited and the research in January favored a frequency count by run for brand names.

    When a loss occurred on Gemini or Copilot, it often meant there was no one cited at all in the response.

    Industry observers note that gemini had responses without citations about 64% of the time in the data from this study, while Copilot showed answers without citations around 53% of the time. Without citations in an answer, a site will appear as a loss when you track your results.

    It has been revealed that many of the comebacks on those two tools were the tool citing sources again after an answer that cited none. With the empty answers left out, Gemini and Copilot looked much like AI Mode and ChatGPT.

    AI Overviews, AI Mode and ChatGPT almost always cited sources. Fewer than 1% of their answers had no citations, and Makosiewicz wrote that a lost citation on those tools almost always means another site took the spot.

    Industry observers note that the first way to verify a lost citation is by looking at the answer. If the answer has no link then you are getting information about the AI tool that day, while if the answer links to a competitor then you have found the site that was cited in your place.

    On Gemini and Copilot, per the write-up, you should keep track of two metrics, the number of times your site gets cited, as well as the frequency with which references are made to another source instead.

    Citations that had stayed active longer before going away were more likely to come back.

    The study ranked all citations on three of the tools (AI Overviews, AI Mode and ChatGPT) in order of how long they had been there until they went away the first time.

    For those with a short life span (one day), 34% to 41% of the citations did not return during the study period.

    And for those that remained there for eight to 14 days, this percentage was at or below 4%.

    In a recent development, this suggests that a citation’s history may be more key than where it stands on a given day. A site referenced once that then disappears is an entirely different circumstance than a site that has maintained its position for 10 days and disappeared yesterday.

    Sources indicate that an analysis of occasional check-in reports shows if a site was cited on a specific date (so every site with only one appearance looks like every other site with continuous appearances). Using a seven-day count allows a team to make a distinction. It counts, for each question being asked, the number of days out of the last seven the site was a source referenced. This shows how often a site turns up. How long one citation held is a separate question.

    This process also provides a team with an ongoing assessment of whether an AI tool is consistently relying on a given site to answer those questions.

    Similarly, it can be applied to upcoming citations. In terms of evaluating the usefulness of a new citation as a lasting win, Makosiewicz suggests waiting a few days before declaring victory. His general rule is to view one missing citation as no reason to change a page, but to review the page if the citation is still missing after two or three weeks.

    A brand can still be named in an answer even after the link to its site disappears.

    Industry observers note that A citation is a link readers can follow. A mention is a brand name in the answer text, whether or not it includes a link.

    Each tool used saw approximately 50% to 70% of all cited sites appear on only one day, as opposed to around one in five of all brands named.

    Sources indicate that then your report can display a lost citation while the answer still names the company. The link is still absent, and it still counts as a lost citation, and looking at the answer will tell you which measure has changed.

    Also, AI tools use different versions (longer or shorter) of the same brand name from answer to answer. And a mention that seems to be gone could be the same company referred to by a different name, so the write-up advises checking for this before subtracting it from your mention totals.

    Since the data showed brand names were not moving nearly as much as citations, Makosiewicz suggests that mentions may be the better metric to follow.

    On AI Overviews and AI Mode, pages that also ranked in Google Search for the same question kept their citations longer.

    In this portion of the study, the authors examined pages. They compared cited pages that appeared somewhere within Google’s results for a question versus those that did not appear anywhere in Google’s results for the same question. On AI Overviews and AI Mode, cited pages that ranked had greater longevity of citation, more often lasting a week or longer; however, the difference between them was smaller for ChatGPT.

    Although appearing in Google’s search results at all correlated with longer-lasting citations more than a page’s exact position in the results list did, according to the write-up, this finding was based on an examination of 230 questions. That comparison showed a correlation between whether pages rank in Google searches for each question and how long the citations to these pages last. Ranking wasn’t a requirement, though. Most of the pages AI Mode and ChatGPT cited didn’t rank in Google for the question they were cited on.

    When a citation stays missing, the authors suggest examining two items, how the page performs in Google Search for the question and how well the page answers the question.

    In September, I proposed a related item to be examined when citations drop while rankings hold steady. That item is to examine the pages being cited in lieu of those originally cited.

    The methodology of this examination also relates to the work performed by SEO teams. When a page loses its Google ranking for a particular question and subsequently drops off of the AI Overview citations, looking into why the page lost its ranking would be a logical starting point to investigate.

    Most citations that disappeared came back during the study, so one comeback alone may not be strong evidence that a page change caused it.

    A team that edits a page after losing a citation and then sees the citation come back has two explanations for it. An edit can’t be credited as working (it may have been due to some other reason) when there is only one comeback to support this.

    Makosiewicz wrote, “Don’t credit a page edit for a single comeback.”.

    In essence, he wants us to look at an increase in the number of times a site reference appears over a longer time span.

    In addition, it would be weak evidence that an edit damaged a citation when that citation disappears the very next day after you edit a page, because half or more of citations disappeared by the next day in the study.

    A number of things can be checked by someone before they change the page behind a lost citation. First, they can look again over the next several days to see whether the citation is still missing. Second, they can read the response itself.

    Management will learn a lot more from a count like five of the last seven, when an in-house team reports how many days a site was cited, than from simply receiving a yes or no from one check.

    An agency has an order to follow on a client call, checking the text of the response, the history of the citation and the ranking of the page prior to making a proposal for upcoming content.

    A content team will get a warning about correlation vs. causation. One comeback after an edit does not provide you with sufficient evidence to make similar edits to other pages.

    The researchers measured the disappearance of citations; they did not test if changing a page brings back a citation that has gone missing.

    Recent findings suggest that they only tracked the very first time a citation went missing. The data collected does not reveal how frequently those same citations disappeared again after returning.

    Industry observers note that the researchers wrote that their figures may represent an underestimate of citations returning as citations that disappeared at the end of the study had less time to return than citations that were lost early in the study. Changes to models could also affect the stability of citation patterns over time.

    Recent findings suggest that the next lost citation will be much easier to read when you have something to reference already. Having a daily log of which sites are cited, related to the questions that matter most, can help provide your team’s own internal tally of days cited prior to a client or manager asking why citations are down.

    When a citation is still missing after two or three weeks, the study’s advice is to look at the page, beginning with how it ranks for the question.

    #113427. Tech Report: A Charity Rescue Dog Outscored Amazon’s Christmas Ad – PPC Accounts Need A Story Before Cyber Week via @sejournal, @gregjarboe

    Tech Report: A Charity Rescue Dog Outscored Amazon’s Christmas Ad – PPC Accounts Need A Story Before Cyber Week via @sejournal, @gregjarboe

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1514 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Searchenginejournal

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that if you run paid media in the United States, the most useful creative test of the 2026 holiday season has already been run for you, on the other side of the Atlantic.
    • You have about two weeks before Cyber Monday and roughly five before Christmas to decide whether your Performance Max and Demand Gen asset groups carry anything that makes people feel something, or just a product carousel and a discount.
    • The rest of this column explains why a UK ad chart matters to a Google Ads account in Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Mississippi, Missouri, or Montana, where I think the data needs ground truthing, and what to change in your accounts this week.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that if you run paid media in the United States, the most useful creative test of the 2026 holiday season has already been run for you, on the other side of the Atlantic. A ranking of 75 U.K. Christmas ads by DAIVID, released Nov. 16, 2026, claims a 60-second charity film about a boy and a scruffy rescue terrier is out-emoting Amazon, John Lewis, and M&S.

    You have about two weeks before Cyber Monday and roughly five before Christmas to decide whether your Performance Max and Demand Gen asset groups carry anything that makes people feel something, or just a product carousel and a discount.

    The rest of this column explains why a UK ad chart matters to a Google Ads account in Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Mississippi, Missouri, or Montana, where I think the data needs ground truthing, and what to change in your accounts this week.

    Industry observers note that start with the money. According to Alphabet’s Q3 2026 earnings release, YouTube ads brought in $11.21 billion of the $82.01 billion in Google advertising revenue for the quarter ended Sept. 30, 2026. That works out to about 13.7%, the same share YouTube held for full-year 2025 ($40.37 billion of $294.69 billion). Across the last four quarters, the share has stayed between 12.8% and 13.8%.

    Search is still Google’s biggest ad business, at $63.35 billion, up 12%. But two remarks from the Oct. 28 earnings call show why creative quality is now a search marketer’s problem, too.

    Google’s CFO Anat Ashkenazi remarked YouTube advertising revenue rose 9%, “with Brand driving the largest contribution.” Brand advertising is exactly what UK Christmas ads are.

    Google’s Chief Business Officer Philipp Schindler said Google has “integrated our AI creative tools directly into AI Max” and that Gemini models “helped advertisers generate over 1.5 billion campaign assets, up over 7x year-over-year.”.

    Google is making creative abundant – when anyone can generate a thousand headlines, images, and video cuts at no extra cost, sheer volume of assets stops being an advantage. What stays scarce is an asset that actually moves people, and that is what DAIVID’s chart tries to measure.

    See also: Why Brand Advertising Matters For Paid Media Performance.

    The conventional wisdom states Brits start Christmas advertising right after Halloween while Americans wait until after Thanksgiving. This year’s data say American advertisers have moved earlier.

    It has been revealed that in a Tatari survey of 41 U.S. TV advertisers, 37% planned to go live in early November and 17% as early as October. Only about one in four planned to wait until Thanksgiving week. Yahoo DSP’s 2026 Holiday Shopping Study, as reported by Chain Store Age, found that 77% of advertisers planned to launch holiday campaigns by November.

    The UK treats Christmas ads as a public event. Hero films drop in early November, the trade press reviews them within days, and testing firms publish scores while the season is still running. U.S. brands rarely publish anything comparable before Black Friday.

    According to recent reports, and most U.S. accounts will head into the peak with old creative. Tatari found only one in five of its advertisers producing net-new Black Friday Cyber Monday spots. A scored set of 75 fresh holiday ads is the closest thing to a free creative pretest you will get this year.

    Amazon’s 2026 film, “Joy Delivered,” is a global campaign that also runs in the U.S., and it placed second in DAIVID’s UK chart.

    See also: How To Evaluate Creative Performance in Meta Ads (and What To Test).

    Dogs Trust’s “Kira Needs A Happy Place,” made by Girl&Bear Studios, the production arm of VCCP Blue, is predicted to trigger intense positive emotions in 58.4% of viewers. DAIVID states that is 20% higher than the average ad. Compared with the average, the film generated more than twice the levels of empathy (+120%), hope (+111%), gratitude (+110%), trust (+106%), and adoration (+102%).

    Amazon’s “Joy Delivered” came second at 55.2%, and Not On The High Street’s “The Birdhouse” came third at 54.0%.

    Lidl UK, Christian Dior, John Lewis, Arsenal FC, M&S, Disney, Barbour, and Shelter fill out the top 10. Gap, TK Maxx, Aldi, and Boots just missed.

    It has been revealed that DAIVID CEO and founder Ian Forrester mentioned, “Dogs Trust has beaten some of the biggest names in advertising by getting one of the fundamentals right: making people feel something. Its story of a boy and his rescue dog generates particularly strong levels of empathy, hope, and adoration, showing that audiences don’t necessarily need spectacle, celebrity, or massive-budget production to connect with a Christmas ad.”.

    Forrester added, “Amazon and Not On The High Street also perform strongly, while the presence of brands such as Lidl, John Lewis, and M&S in the top ten reveals there are different ways to make an emotional connection with audiences.”.

    Dogs Trust is a charity, and the star of its film is a real rescue dog.

    See also: How To Run Profitable YouTube Ad Campaign Without 7-Figure Budgets.

    It has been revealed that I apply the same test to an ad-testing vendor that I apply to Google’s own performance claims. What exactly is being measured, and how big are the differences?

    According to recent reports, start with the fact that these are predictions. DAIVID’s methodology states its AI models, trained on tens of millions of human responses to ads, forecast how viewers would feel.

    It has been revealed that nobody sat a fresh panel in front of “Kira.” That makes the chart fast and cheap, which is the point. It also means DAIVID’s claim of performance improvements above 20% is the vendor’s claim, not an independent finding.

    The spread is narrow, too. Dogs Trust leads Amazon by 3.2 points. Below the top three places, four through joint 10th sit within 0.9 points of one another, from 53.7% down to 52.8%. I would not tell a client that Lidl beat John Lewis on the strength of 0.3 points.

    It has been revealed that last year’s DAIVID, Disney’s “Best Christmas Ever,” scored 58.2%. This year’s winner scored 58.4%. Even the best Christmas storytelling in Britain leaves about four in ten viewers short of intense positive emotion.

    My view is that this chart is most useful as a creative brief rather than a leaderboard. The winners share a pattern you can copy into an asset group tomorrow. A simple story. A character the viewer roots for. Very little product on screen until late. And the emotions a discount banner can’t produce, especially hope, gratitude, and trust.

    Here is what I would do with the time left before Cyber Week.

    It has been revealed that audit Your Asset Groups For A Story: Open your Performance Max asset groups and Demand Gen campaigns and look at the video assets. If you haven’t uploaded a video, Performance Max can build one from your images and text, and it will look like it. Add at least one advertiser-made video, even a 15- or 30-second cut, which tells a small human story before it shows a product. Then review what Gemini generated for you. With 1.5 billion assets coming off the line, the default output drifts toward the same product-on-white look your competitors are getting.

    Test Story Against Offer, With A Real Control: Set up a Demand Gen A/B experiment that splits traffic between an emotional cut and your standard offer-led creative. Keep audiences, bidding, and budgets identical so creative is the only variable. Ten days won’t settle it, so initiative to run the test through the December shipping deadlines and read conversion volume alongside cost per conversion.

    Industry observers note that watch Branded Search As The Bridge Metric: Brand ads earn their keep in a search account by creating demand you harvest later. Before the story asset goes live, record your branded query volume, branded impression share, and branded conversions, then check them weekly through December. If you meet the spend thresholds, a Brand Lift study with search lift will give you Google’s read on whether the video drove searches for your brand. Treat that as Google’s measurement, and compare it with what your branded Search campaigns actually show.

    Recent findings suggest that rerun What Has Already Worked: Amazon reran its 2023 film “Joy Ride” as its 2025 holiday hero ad after it tested strongly, and shifted the production savings into media, according to DesignRush. If you have a past holiday video that performed, put it back into Demand Gen and Performance Max rather than replacing it with a weaker new cut made to hit a deadline.

    According to recent reports, I have covered paid search since 2003, and for most of that time the industry optimized the parts of an ad a machine could measure, like bids, keywords, and landing pages. Google’s AI now automates those parts and fills accounts with generated creative. That leaves one input a PPC manager still controls, which is whether the creative makes anyone care.

    A rescue terrier outscored Amazon this year. Your holiday budget deserves at least one asset that tries.

    #113420. Google’s ‘Top 10’ Line For CMOs Points At Generic Tips Posts via @sejournal, @MattGSouthern

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (588 w)

    Google’s ‘Top 10’ Line For CMOs Points At Generic Tips Posts via @sejournal, @MattGSouthern

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (588 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Searchenginejournal

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Google told CMOs through its Think with Google account on Nov.
    • The post pairs “Stop the ‘Top 10’ listicle” with “start leading with first-hand expertise.” That first half drew questions from SEOs on X about whether Google is telling brands to drop listicles.
    • It has been revealed that the article appeared Oct.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Google told CMOs through its Think with Google account on Nov. 19 that “AI didn’t make your brand invisible in Search. Your content did.”.

    The post pairs “Stop the ‘Top 10’ listicle” with “start leading with first-hand expertise.” That first half drew questions from SEOs on X about whether Google is telling brands to drop listicles. The October article the post links to is more specific. Its example is a generic “Top 10 Things to Consider” post, the same kind of post Google Search’s own AI guide cites as commodity content.

    It has been revealed that the article appeared Oct. 14 on Think with Google, the tech giant’s digital marketing publication. Written by Brendon Kraham, Google’s VP, Search & Commerce Global Ads Solutions, it encourages brands to create specific content that draws on their own expertise and to measure their plans by leads or sales.

    Kraham structures the article around three top priorities that he has heard from CMOs, which cover the “super-empowered consumer,” establishing the brand as an authority in its area of expertise, and creating measurable business results.

    Think with Google summarized its advice to CMOs in this three-point cheat sheet.

    The “Top 10” reference is found in his section on developing expertise, where he writes:.

    Sources indicate that take a running store, for example. Instead of publishing a generic “Top 10 Things to Consider,” they could create a deep-dive video analyzing exactly why a specific customer’s running shoes collapsed. That isn’t a generic review anyone could have written. It’s highly specific, real-world advice.

    On measurement, he tells CMOs to keep planning “based on real business goals like leads or sales, not unproven proxy metrics.”.

    Lily Ray, who founded Algorythmic and specializes in SEO and AI search strategy, referenced the post on X and exclaimed, “Wow did Google really just tell CMOs to stop with the top 10 listicles?”.

    It has been revealed that ray is no stranger to tracking self-promotional “best” listicles, where a tech giant lists itself as #1. In a June column for Search Engine Journal, she also reported that many of Google’s AI Overview results cited such listicles along with recommendations for other companies.

    Growth advisor Eli Schwartz posted his version of the three steps “without being sanitized by the PR team.” Next to “Stop trusting proxy scores,” his post reads, “AEO VISIBILITY IS NOT REAL.”.

    Ross Hudgens, founder and CEO of Siege Media, replied to Ray, “Not of the type you’re thinking of. :)”.

    Sources indicate that google Search’s guide to optimizing for generative AI features, published in May, draws the same line as Kraham’s article. It gives “7 Tips for First-Time Homebuyers” as an example of commodity content, which it states is “often based on common knowledge.” The guide contrasts it with a first-hand piece about waiving a home inspection.

    Neither the article nor the guide mentions self-promotional “best” lists.

    When this content from Google reaches a CMO, the article it links to provides the recommendations in detail; it also has the same criteria for evaluating planned tips posts as does Google Search’s guide. Go through each of these individually, first asking if each represents something you have learned firsthand or simply restates common knowledge.

    For self-promotional “best” lists, look to Ray’s tracking data instead.

    Recent findings suggest that google shares major updates to its Search documentation on the documentation updates page, which also offers an RSS feed. Following the feed is an easy way to keep up with changes as they’re posted.

    Featured Image: Remo_Designer/Shutterstock.

With built-in governance, auditability, and human oversight, Camunda gives enterprises the control they need to move AI from pilots to production — safely and at scale. If you want meaningful work, visible impact and put something genuinely rare on your CV, keep reading.

    It has been revealed that camunda Hub is where enterprises run Camunda at scale. From Hub they manage their clusters and tenants, decide who can do what, and roll changes out across the whole organization. We’re looking for a Senior Product Builder to own the backend and architecture that let Hub manage a whole fleet of clusters. Your first focus will be the mechanism that sends access, secret, tenant and licence changes out to every connected cluster and brings deployments, health and audit records back. From there, you’ll shape Hub’s foundations: its event model, the service boundaries and data model other teams build on, and how Hub behaves when things fail or get upgraded. The platform is your product. Your consumers are platform administrators, Centres of Excellence and the builders across Camunda who depend on what you create. You’ll join a new two-person pod in our remote-first team. You’ll have real ownership as the person who makes the call, and you’ll build AI-first, from written specs through to production. Our customers run mission-critical processes on Camunda, so your work will matter to them every day.

    Take over Hub's fleet propagation mechanism from the team building its first version, and make it work for access, secrets, tenants, licences and custom roles.

    Write short design documents for foundational changes, get them reviewed by the teams that depend on them, and turn them into tested, shipped code.

    Design how Hub behaves when things go wrong: offline clusters, partial failures, Hub outages, and clusters being adopted or detached.

    Build the path from clusters back to Hub, starting with deployment inventory, health, audit records and licence status.

    Design Hub's first event and webhook mechanism, so admins and agents can react to changes instead of polling for them.

    Join the pod's rotations and Hub on-call, and help other builders take on backend work through reviews, guidelines and contract tests.

    What You Will Bring to the Role:.

    Experience building and running backend systems in production that other teams or customers depend on.

    Comfort taking a problem nobody owns yet and turning it into a design, a strategy and shipped code.

    Product judgment for technical owners: you talk to the people who use your APIs and make trade-offs on their behalf.

    Clear, short writing that lets a remote team review and decide asynchronously.

    Care for how a system behaves when parts of it fail, not only for the happy path.

    Industry observers note that designed and shipped a control plane or similar system that pushes desired state to many targets. Knows outbox or event-log patterns, idempotent apply, versioning, retries and drift reconciliation.

    Senior backend engineering in Java (API design, relational data models, multi-tenant SaaS services) and hands-on Helm and Kubernetes for self-managed installations.

    Software architecture and failure analysis: partial failure, blast radius, consistency trade-offs. Has debugged production incidents in a distributed system and is ready for on-call.

    Has shaped an API or platform as a product, and writes design docs other teams can build on. Gets agreement across teams without formal authority.

    Builds AI-first from written specifications and checks AI output as carefully as any other code.

    Kubernetes operators or GitOps tools, for example Argo CD.

    OIDC, SCIM and permission models, or secret managers and licence systems.

    Camunda 8 or another workflow or orchestration engine.

    Enough frontend skill to build a thin UI on top of a backend capability.
